title: About Justin Morrie Sacdalan
description: Meet Justin Morrie Sacdalan: Computer Science student, developer and digital creative at De La Salle University.

hero.eyebrow: A LITTLE ABOUT ME / JUSTIN MORRIE SACDALAN
hero.headline: Keep on keeping on
hero.accent: Until it's done, and done right.
hero.lede: Cheers! I'm Justin, a Computer Science student at De La Salle University in the Philippines. I like making things—and figuring out how to make them better while having fun.
hero.caption: web · software · digital media

sections.label: MORE ABOUT ME
sections.heading: My AGENT.md
sections.body:
If I had to write a quick guide to working with me, it would start with this: I don't take things at face value. Whether it's a dataset, a bug, or one of the many app ideas living rent-free in my head, I like to study it first, which is why most of my time goes into planning and setting things up. Give me a clear goal and a deadline, and it'll get done. Just know that I'll probably keep nitpicking the details until it actually feels right (perfectionism is both my strength and my biggest time sink).

Outside of coding, I'm into a lot of things, honestly. I build mechanical keyboards and Magic: The Gathering decks, practice my coffee-making (someday I'd love to run my own café), and window-shop PCs and laptops I definitely can't afford yet. I also play more gacha games than I'd like to admit, grind through Warframe and Monster Hunter, and binge manga and manhwa before chasing down the novels they came from.

Most of these interests sneak into my work one way or another. A few of my projects hide small references to the games and stories I love, so if you catch one, it'll probably make my day. If not, that's totally fine too (my tastes are kinda niche).

sections.label: ABOUT MY PROJECTS
sections.heading: Well of Ideas.
sections.body:
I’ve been drawn to the space between technology and digital creativity for as long as I can remember. Whether it’s a web app, an interface, a video, or some random idea that just popped into my head, I like taking that first rough concept and turning it into something people can actually use (or at least have fun with).

Most of my work lives on the web, where I build with React, Next.js and TypeScript, though I’ve also picked up JavaScript, Python and Kotlin along the way. I care just as much about how an interface feels as how it works behind the scenes, which is usually where the nitpicking starts.

Some of my favorites so far are [Gastos.io](/work/gastos-io), a personal expense tracker, and [Pocket Gains](/work/pocket-gains), a workout tracker that turns your progress into a game. Both started as one of those many app ideas, and both taught me something new before they were done.

sections.label: MORE THAN CODE
sections.heading: Building for people.
sections.body:
I’m part of **The LaSallian’s Web team**, where I help build and maintain the website of DLSU’s student publication. Working alongside writers and editors has given me a new appreciation for clear, accessible design and the people behind everything that ends up on screen.

Outside of code, I also do graphic design, video editing and short-form content. I handle my social media on my own, and one of my TikTok channels has picked up around **1.9 million views and 11,100 likes** (still kinda surreal to me). Watching an idea click with an audience is just as fulfilling as finally seeing a project come together.

I’ve also been part of the **La Salle Computer Society** and the **DLSU Data Science Society**, which pulled me out of my comfort zone and into events, collaborations and a lot of people who are just as curious as I am.

sections.label: HOW I WORK
sections.heading: Ask better questions.
sections.body:
If there’s one thing that describes how I work, it’s that I like figuring things out. I don’t really trust the first answer I get, so I’d rather understand *why* something works, question the assumptions behind it, and try another approach if the result could be better.

I don’t think being good at something means knowing every answer. For me, it means knowing how to ask the right questions, finding reliable information, and making the most of whatever tools and “resources” I have on hand. Honestly, that’s pretty much how I’ve learned most of what I know.

contact.label: WHAT’S NEXT
contact.heading: Let’s make something happen.
contact.body: I’m always open to interesting projects, creative collaborations, or just learning something new from a different perspective. Have something in mind? Let’s talk.
